questions.q: A particle is moving in a circular path with a constant speed $v$. If $\theta$ is the angular displacement. Then starting from $\theta=0$, the maximum and minimum changes in the momentum will occur, when value of $\theta$ is respectively:
questions.solution:
When $\theta=180^{\circ}$, the particle will be at diametrically opposite point. Where its velocity is opposite to the direction of motion.
The change in momentum $=m v-(-m v)+2 m v$ (maximum).
When $\theta=360^{\circ}$, the particle is at the initial position with momentum $m v$ change in momentum $=m v-m v=0$ (minimum).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: A ball falls vertically on to a floor, with momentum $p$, and then bounces repeatedly, the coefficient of restitution is $e$. The total momentum imparted by the ball to the floor is
questions.solution:
When a particle undergoes normal collision with a floor or a wall, with coefficient of restitution $e$, the speed after collision is e times the speed before collision. Therefore, change in momentum after Ist impact is $e p-(-p)=p(1+e)$
After the second impact, change in momentum would be $e(e p)-(-e p)=e p(1+e)$ and soon. Therefore, total change in momentum of ball $\begin{aligned} & =p(1+e)\left[1+e+e^2+\ldots\right] \\ & =p\left(\frac{1+e}{1-e}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If an electron has an initial velocity in a direction different from that of an electric field, the path of the electron is :
questions.solution: The path is a parabola, because initial velocity can be resolved into two rectangular components, one along $\vec{E}$ and other perpendicular to $\vec{E}$. The former decreases at a constant rate and later is unaffected. The resultant path is, therefore a parabola.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Imagine a light planet revolving around a very massive star in a circular orbit of radius $R$ with a period of revolution $T$. If the gravitational force of attraction between the planet and the star is proportional to $R^{-5 / R}$, then $T^2$ is proportional to :
questions.solution:
Gravitational force $\left(=\frac{G M m}{R^{5 / 2}}\right)$ provides the necessary centripetal force $\left(i e, m R \omega^2\right)$. So,
$\frac{G M m}{R^{5 / 2}}=m R \omega^2=m R\left(\frac{2 \pi}{T}\right)^2=\frac{4 \pi^2 m R}{T^2}$
or
$T^2=\frac{4 \pi^2 R^{7 / 2}}{G M}$
i.e,
$T^2 \propto R^{7 / 2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A satellite goes along an elliptical path arounds earth. The rate of change of area swept by the same line joining earth and the satellite is proportional to :

Areal velocity $=\frac{d A}{d t}=\frac{L}{2 m}=\frac{m v r}{2 m}=\frac{v r}{2}=\frac{r}{2} \sqrt{\frac{G M}{r}}=\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{G M r}$
So, $\frac{d A}{d t} \propto \sqrt{r}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical cylinders contain helium at 2.5 atm and argon at 1 atm respectively. If both the gases are filled in one of the cylinders, the pressure would be :
questions.solution:
Total pressure, when the two gases are filled in one cylinder is equal to sum of the pressures of the individual gases.
Thus, total pressure $=2.5+1=3.5 \mathrm{~atm}$

The spring of length $l_1\left(=n l_2\right)$ will be equivalent to $n$ springs connected in series where spring constant
$k^{\prime \prime}=\frac{k^{\prime}}{n}=\frac{(n+1) k}{n}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fireman weighing 80 kg slides down a pole. If the resisting force of friction is 720 N , his acceleration would be : (take $\left.g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
Force of friction $=720 \mathrm{~N}$
If $a$ is the acceleration of fireman, sliding down the pole, then
$\begin{aligned} m g-F & =m a \\ a & =\frac{m g-F}{m} \\ & =\frac{(80 \times 10-720)}{80} \\ & =1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A 4 kg block $A$ is placed on the top of a block $B$ of mass 8 kg , which rests on a smooth table. A just slips on $B$ when a force of 12 N is applied on $A$.
Then, the maximum horizontal force required to make both $A$ and $B$ move together is :

The mass of block $A=4 \mathrm{~kg}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force of 5 N gives a mass $M_1$ an acceleration equal to $8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ and $M_2$ an acceleration equal to $24 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$. What is the acceleration, if both masses are tied together ?
questions.solution:
Mass $M_1=\frac{5}{8} \mathrm{~kg}$, Mass $M_2=\frac{5}{24} \mathrm{~kg}$
Total maks $=M_1+M_2=\frac{5}{8}+\frac{5}{24}=\frac{20}{24} \mathrm{~kg}$
Therefore, total acceleration in two masses
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{F}{M_1+M_2}=\frac{5}{20 / 24} \\ & =\frac{5 \times 24}{20}=6 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two wires $P Q$ and $Q R$, carry equal currents I as shown in figure. One end of both the wires extends to infinity $\angle P Q R=\theta$. The magnitude of the magnetic field at $O$ on the bisector of these two wires at a distance $r$ from point $O$ is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A bar magnet has a magnetic moment equal to $5 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~Wb}-\mathrm{m}$. It is suspended in a magnetising field equal to $8 \pi \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~A}-\mathrm{m}^{-1}$.
The magnet vibrates with a period 15 s . The moment of inertia of the magnet is:
questions.solution:
The SI unit of magnetic moment is $\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{m}^2$, but the magnetic moment is given in $\mathrm{Wb}-\mathrm{m}^2$, which is the unit of $\mu_0 M$.
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \mu_0 M & =5 \times 10^{-5} \\ M & =\frac{5 \times 10^{-5}}{\mu_0} \mathrm{~Wb}-\mathrm{m} \\ & =\frac{5 \times 10^{-5}}{4 \pi \times 10^{-7}}=\frac{125}{\pi}\end{aligned}$
As
$T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{I}{M B}}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad I & =\frac{T^2 M B}{4 \pi^2}=\frac{(15)^2\left(\frac{125}{\pi}\right) \times 8 \pi \times 10^{-4}}{4 \pi^2} \\ & =0.57 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A copper wire of diameter 1.6 mm carries a current $I$. The maximum magnetic field due to this wire is $5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~T}$. The value of $l$ is :

Maximum magnetic field due to wire carrying current is at surface and is given by
$B=\frac{\mu_0}{4 \pi} \frac{2 l}{R}$
or $\quad I=\frac{B R}{2 \times\left(\mu_0 / 4 \pi\right)}\therefore \quad I=\frac{5 \times 10^{-4} \times\left(\frac{1.6 \times 10^{-3}}{2}\right)}{2 \times 10^{-7}}=2 \mathrm{~A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To what height should a rectangular cylinder having square base of length 10 cm be filled, so that the total force on the bottom is equal to that on the sides ?
questions.solution:
If $h$ is the height of liquid column in cylinder and $I$ is the length of each side of base. Then
$\begin{aligned} & F_B=(h \rho g)(I \times l)=h \rho g l^2 \\ & F_S=\left(\frac{h \rho g}{2}\right)(4 I \times h)=2 h^2 \rho g l\end{aligned}\therefore \quad h \rho g l^2=2 h^2 \rho g l$
or $h=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{10}{2}=5 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: A steel ring of radius $r$ and cross-sectional area $A$ is fitted on to a wooden disc of radius $R(R \gt r)$. If Young's modulus be $Y$, then the force with which the steel ring is expanded, is
questions.solution:
Strain $=\frac{\Delta l}{l}=\frac{2 \pi R-2 \pi r}{2 \pi r}=\left(\frac{R-r}{r}\right)$
Stress $=Y \times$ strain $=\frac{F}{A}\therefore \quad F=Y \times A \times$ strain $=A Y \times\left(\frac{R-r}{r}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A point initially at rest moves along $x$-axis. Its acceleration varies with time as $a=(6 t+5)$ in $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$. If it starts from origin, the distance covered in 2 s is :
questions.solution:
Given, $a=\frac{d v}{d t}=6 t+5$ Integrating it, $\int_0^v d v=\int_0^t(6 t+5) d tv=\frac{6 t^2}{2}+5 t$
As $\quad v=\frac{d s}{d t}$, so $d s=\left(\frac{6 t^2}{2}+5 t\right) d t$ Integrating it, $\int_0^s d s=\int_0^t\left(\frac{6 t^2}{2}+5 t\right) d ts=\frac{3 t^3}{3}+\frac{5 t^2}{2}$
When  $\begin{aligned} t & =2 \mathrm{~s}, s=3 \frac{(2)^3}{3}+\frac{5(2)^2}{2} \\ & =8+10=18 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics

= 2 m/s

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a horizontal circle of radius $R$ under the centripetal force $=-k / R^2$ where $k$ is a constant. What is the total energy of the particle?
questions.solution: Centripetal force $=\frac{m v^2}{R}=\frac{k}{R^2}($ in magnitude $)\therefore \quad \mathrm{KE}=\frac{1}{2} m v^2=\frac{1}{2} \frac{k}{R}P E=-\int F d R=-\int \frac{-k}{R^2} d R=-\frac{k}{R}\therefore$ Total energy $=\mathrm{KE}+\mathrm{PE}=\frac{k}{2 R}-\frac{k}{R}=-\frac{k}{2 R}$

questions.q: A particle is projected from the ground with an initial speed of $u$ at an angle $\theta$ with horizontal. The average velocity of the particle between its point of projection and highest point of trajectory is :
questions.solution:
Refer figure as shown, the average velocity
$=\frac{\text { displacement }}{\text { time taken }}v_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{\sqrt{H^2+R^2 / 4}}{T / 2}$...(i) Here, $H=\frac{u^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 g}R=\frac{u^2 \sin 2 \theta}{g}$ Putting these values in Eq. (i), we get $v_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{u}{2} \sqrt{1+3 \cos ^2 \theta}$

questions.q: A wave travelling in a stretched string is described by the equation $y=A \sin (k x-\omega t)$. The maximum particle velocity is :
questions.solution: $\begin{gathered}y=A \sin (k x-\omega t) \\ \frac{d y}{d t}=A \cos (k x-\omega t) \times(\omega) \\ \left(\frac{d y}{d t}\right)_{\max }=A(1)(\omega)=A \omega\end{gathered}$

questions.q: A mass $M$ is attached to a string, oscillates with a period of 2 s . If the mass is increased by 4 kg . The time period increases by 1 s . Assuming, that Hooke's law is obeyed, the initial mass $M$ was :
questions.solution:
$T=2=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{M}{k}}$
and  $2+1=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{M+4}{k}}$
or  $3=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{M+4}{k}}\therefore \quad \frac{4}{9}=\frac{M}{M+4}$
or  $4 M+16=9 M$
or  $M=\frac{16}{5}=3.2 \mathrm{~kg}$

questions.q: If $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}}$ are the unit vectors along the incident ray, reflected ray and outward normal to the reflecting surface, then:
questions.solution:
Let $\vec{A}, \vec{B}$ and $\vec{C}$ be as shown in figure. Let $\theta$ be the angle of incidence, which is equal to the angle of reflection. Resolving these vectors in rectangular components, we have

$\begin{aligned} \overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}} & =\sin \theta \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ \overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}} & =\sin \theta \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}} \\ \overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}-\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}} & =2 \cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}}\end{aligned}$ or $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}=\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}}+2 \cos \theta \hat{\mathbf{j}}$ Now, $\quad \overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}}=(1)(1) \cos \left(180^{\circ}-\theta\right)=-\cos \theta\therefore \quad \vec{B}=\vec{A}-2(\vec{A} \cdot \vec{C}) \hat{j}$ or $\vec{B}=\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}}-2(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}}) \overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}}($ as $\hat{j}=\overrightarrow{\mathbf{C}})$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of radius $R$ has moment of inertia / about its diameter. What will be moment of inertia of a shell of same mass and same radius about its diameter ?
questions.solution:
For a solid sphere, $I=\frac{2}{5} M R^2$
For a spherical shell, $\begin{aligned} I^{\prime} & =\frac{2}{3} M R^2 \\ & =\frac{5}{3} \times \frac{2}{5} M R^2=\frac{5}{3} I\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform thin bar of mass 6 m and length $12 L$ is bent to make a regular hexagon. Its moment of inertia about an axis passing through the centre of mass and perpendicular to the plane of hexagon is :
questions.solution:
Length of each side of hexagon $=2 L$ and mass of each side $=m$
Let $O$ be the centre of mass of hexagon. Therefore, perpendicular distance of $O$ from each side, $r=L \tan 60^{\circ}=L \sqrt{3}$ The desired moment of inertia of hexagon about $O$ is $\begin{aligned} I & =6\left[I_{\text {one side }}\right]=6\left[\frac{m(2 L)^2}{12}+m r^2\right] \\ & =6\left[\frac{mL^2}{3}+m(L \sqrt{3})^2\right] \\ & =20 mL^2\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is projected with a velocity $v$ at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with horizontal. When the particle is at its maximum height, the magnitude of its angular momentum about the point of projection is :
questions.solution:
Maximum height
$H=\frac{v^2 \sin ^2 45^{\circ}}{2 g}=\frac{v^2}{2 g} \times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{v^2}{4 g}$
Momentum of particle at the highest point
$p=m v \cos 45^{\circ}=m v / \sqrt{2}$
Angular momentum $=\mathrm{pH}=\frac{m v}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{v^2}{4 g}=\frac{m v^3}{4 \sqrt{2} g}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The rays of sun are focussed on a piece of ice through a lens of diameter 5 cm , as a result of which 10 g ice melts in 10 min . The amount of heat received from sun, per unit area per minute is :
questions.solution:
Mass of ice melted per minute $=\frac{10}{10}=1 \mathrm{~g}\begin{aligned} & \text { Quantity of heat used } \\ & \qquad \begin{aligned} \text {Area of lens } & =\pi r^2 \\ & =19.625 \mathrm{~cm}^2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}\therefore$ Amount of heat received from sun
$=\frac{80}{19.625}=4 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{cm}^2 \mathrm{~min}$
Latent heat of fusion $=80$

questions.q: A thin copper wire of length $L$ increases in length by $1 \%$, when heated from $T_1$ to $T_2$. What is the percentage change in area when a thin copper plate having dimensions $(10 L \times 2 L)$ is heated from $T_1$ to $T_2$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} A & =10 L \times 2 L=20 L^2 \\ \frac{\Delta A}{A} \times 100 & =2 \frac{\Delta L}{L} \times 100=2 \times 1=2 \%\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: $\eta=\frac{W}{Q_1}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad w & =\eta Q_1=\frac{1}{3} \times 1000 \mathrm{cal} \\ & =\frac{1000}{3} \times 4.2 \mathrm{~J}=1400 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: During an adiabatic process, the pressure $P$ of a fixed mass of an ideal gas changes by $\Delta P$ and its volume $V$ changes by $\Delta V$. If $\gamma=C_P / C_V$, then $\Delta V / V$ is given by:
questions.solution: $K_{\text {adia }}=\gamma P=-\frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V / V}\therefore \quad \frac{\Delta V}{V}=-\frac{\Delta P}{\gamma P}$

questions.q: 8 g of $\mathrm{O}_2, 14 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{N}_2$, and 2 g of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is mixed in a container of 10 L capacity at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The pressure exerted by the mixture in terms of atmospheric pressure is $\left(R=0.082 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~atm} \mathrm{k}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right):$
questions.solution: $P=\frac{n_1 R T+n_2 R T+n_3 R T}{V}=\left(n_1+n_2+n_3\right) \frac{R T}{V}\begin{aligned} & =\left(\frac{8}{16}+\frac{14}{28}+\frac{22}{44}\right) \times \frac{0.082 \times 300}{10} \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\right) \times 2.46 \\ & =\frac{3}{2} \times 2.46=3.69 \mathrm{~atm} \approx 3.7 \mathrm{~atm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The displacement of an oscillating particle is given by $y=A \sin [B x+C t+D t]$. The dimensional formula for $[A B C D]$ is :
questions.solution:
$y=A \sin [B x+C t+D]$
As each term inside the bracket is dimension less, $\therefore \quad[A]=[y]=[L], \quad[B]=\frac{1}{[x]}=\left[L^{-1}\right]$
$[C]=\frac{1}{[t]}=\left[1^{-1}\right]$ and $D$ is dimensionless. $\therefore[A B C D]=[\mathrm{L}]\left[\mathrm{L}^{-1}\right]\left[\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right][1]=\left[\mathrm{N}^0 \mathrm{~L}^0 \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A heavy uniform rope hangs vertically from the ceiling, with its lower end free. A disturbance on the rope travelling upwards from the lower end has a velocity $v$ at a distance $x$ from the lower end such that :
questions.solution:
Let $m=$ mass per unit length of rope
$T=$ tension in the rope at a distance $x$ from the lower end
$\therefore T=(\mathrm{mg}) \mathrm{x}=$ weight of $x$ metre of rope
As  $v=\sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}\therefore \quad v=\sqrt{\frac{m g x}{m}}=\sqrt{g x}$
i.e., $\quad v \propto \sqrt{x}$

questions.q: A stretched sonometer wire is in unison with a tuning fork. When length of wire is increase by $1 \%$, the number of beats heard per second is 5. Then the frequency of the fork is :
questions.solution:
Let frequency of tuning fork be $n_1\frac{n_2}{n_1}=\frac{100}{101}$
As $n_1-n_2=5$
So, $n_1=505 \mathrm{~Hz}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The displacement $x$ and time $t$ for a particle are related to each other as $t=\sqrt{x}+3$. What is work done in first 6 s of its motion ?
questions.solution:
$t=\sqrt{x}+3$
or $\quad x=(t-3)^2$
Now, $\quad v=\frac{d x}{d t}=2(t-3)$
At $t=0, v_1=2(-3)=-6$
At $\quad t=6, v_2=2(6-3)=6$
Work done = change in KE
$=\frac{1}{2} m v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} m v_1^2=0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object $A$ moving horizontally with kinetic energy of 800 J experiences a constant opposing force of 100 N , while moving from a place $x$ to a place $y$, where $x y$ is 2 m . What is the energy of $A$ at $y$ ?
questions.solution: Energy at $y=$ total KE - work done from $x$ to $y=800-100 \times 2=600 \mathrm{~J}$
